assumptions: No explicit initial state was specified, so the initial state is chosen as the first listed FSM state: increase.

The continuous wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, slip-ratio, and PID computations are abstracted as an external slip-error input variable `slp`; only the discrete Stateflow-style supervisor and hydraulic command outputs are modeled in this DSL candidate.

transition guards split the slip-error space into four bands using `slp` thresholds

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init dispatches to increase with inlet-valve command, then at slp=0.01 the increase-to-hold boundary guard neutralizes valves.
scenario_results.name: default_init_increase_then_hold_at_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in increase with slp just above 0.01 must not take the increase-to-hold guard.
scenario_results.name: increase_no_fire_above_upper_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in hold with slp greater than 0.01 must transition to increase and set inlet-valve outputs.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_increase_above_upper_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in hold with slp exactly 0.01 must not satisfy the strict hold-to-increase guard.
scenario_results.name: hold_no_fire_at_upper_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in hold with slp below -0.01 must transition to decrease and command pressure release.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_decrease_below_lower_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in hold with slp exactly -0.01 must not satisfy the strict hold-to-decrease guard.
scenario_results.name: hold_no_fire_at_lower_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in decrease with slp exactly -0.01 must transition to hold and neutralize both valves.
scenario_results.name: decrease_to_hold_at_lower_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in decrease with slp below -0.01 must not satisfy the decrease-to-hold guard and must keep pressure-release outputs.
scenario_results.name: decrease_no_fire_below_lower_boundary

evidence: NL states: increase sets k1=1,k2=0,n=0; hold sets k1=0,k2=0,n=0; decrease sets k1=0,k2=1,n=500.
DSL implements states increase, hold, decrease with matching enter actions.
NL transition guards: increase->hold slp<=0.01, hold->increase slp>0.01, hold->decrease slp<-0.01, decrease->hold slp>=-0.01.
DSL implements the same four guarded transitions.
findings.summary: The DSL faithfully captures the explicitly enumerated three-state hydraulic supervisor, state output actions, and four slip-error threshold transitions from the NL.

evidence: NL says wheel speed and vehicle speed are used to compute slip ratio, and PID output drives the Stateflow supervisor.
DSL declares only slp, k1, k2, and n; no wheel speed, vehicle speed, slip-ratio computation, PID state, PID output, or controller gains are represented.
GroundingMap source_summary explicitly assumes continuous wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, slip-ratio, and PID computations are abstracted as external slip-error input slp.
findings.summary: The discrete FSM component is well covered, but the PID, wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, and slip-ratio computation components are abstracted into a single external slp variable rather than modeled as separate components.

evidence: GroundingMap assumption: no explicit initial state was specified, so the initial state is chosen as the first listed FSM state: increase.
DSL contains [*] -> increase.
NL enumerates states and transitions but does not specify the initial state.
findings.summary: The initial state is assumed as increase without direct NL evidence.

evidence: NL describes a three-state FSM coupled with a PID-based slip controller.
DSL models only the three-state FSM and hydraulic command outputs.
GroundingMap states the continuous/plant/process dynamics and PID computations are outside the DSL candidate.
findings.summary: The model is intentionally simplified to the discrete Stateflow-style supervisor; this is acceptable for the stated supervisor scope but should not be treated as a complete ABS controller model.

evidence: Diagnostics include W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR for slp and W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE for guards reading slp.
design_diagnostics_summary.nl_external_input_vars lists slp.
external_input_role_ledger identifies slp as an external_input_candidate.
Diagnostics include W_UNREFERENCED_VAR for k1, k2, and n, which are pure hydraulic outputs rather than guard variables.
findings.summary: The DSL does not explicitly type variable roles as external input versus pure outputs, causing advisory diagnostics even though the intended roles are recoverable from NL grounding.

evidence: Required states, state actions, transitions, and guards from the discrete supervisor are present.
design_diagnostics_summary.ok is true with blocking_count 0.
sim_summary.ok is true with 8 of 8 scenarios passed.
Remaining issues are scope abstraction and role annotation, not missing required FSM states/transitions/guards/actions.
findings.summary: No blocking NFRR quality cap is warranted. Estimated tier: T2 within-scope candidate, approaching T3 for the discrete supervisor only.

evidence: sim_summary reports 8 scenarios and 8 passed.
Scenario samples cover upper and lower threshold boundaries and non-firing cases.
No scenarios cover wheel-speed/vehicle-speed slip computation or PID output behavior.
findings.summary: Simulation coverage is targeted to the stated threshold behavior and passes, but the oracle is limited to the discrete FSM abstraction and does not evaluate PID/plant coupling.

evidence: GroundingMap elements cover all states, guards, transitions, and output actions with high confidence.
GroundingMap source_summary records an abstraction assumption for PID and continuous dynamics.
five_component_summary is empty, so there is no independent component-level corroboration of the abstraction boundary.
findings.summary: Grounding is strong for the discrete supervisor but weaker for the abstraction boundary because the NL mentions coupled PID behavior while the DSL represents only slp as an external input.
